codeReview.summary: The Tabs implementation is well-structured, follows established component patterns (options pattern, theme tokens, no raw colors), and fully covers all VAL-CMP-006 requirements. The active indicator uses colored underline (━ in Accent/AccentMuted) plus Accent foreground on the active label — clearly not font-weight-only. Keyboard navigation supports →/←/h/l, Tab/Shift-Tab, Home/End/g/G with configurable wrap-around. 27 unit tests + 5 snapshot tests provide thorough coverage. Two minor non-blocking issues noted.

issues.description: moveFirst() and moveLast() unconditionally fire onChange even when already at the first/last tab. This means Home/End/g/G always triggers the callback regardless of whether the active index actually changed. Other components typically guard with `if t.activeIdx != newIdx { ... fireOnChange() }`. Low impact since consumers can debounce or check, but it's a minor behavioral inconsistency.

In the single-tab branch (n <= 1), there's a dead code check for Shift+Tab at line 104: `evt.Key == tui.KeyTab && evt.Mod.Has(tui.ModShift)`. This can never be reached because line 93 already matched `evt.Key == tui.KeyTab` without the shift check. The earlier match consumes all KeyTab events before reaching this block. This is harmless but mildly confusing for readers.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The component spec says inactive tab text should use `TextSecondary` color token, but the implementation uses `TextMuted` instead. The spec field table (§1) doesn't explicitly name the inactive color — it just says inactive tabs should be 'plain'. However, the component spec's general focus indicator rules (§10) refer to `TextMuted` for inactive elements in other widgets. This seems like a reasonable interpretation but creates a discrepancy between spec text and implementation that could confuse future workers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: component-spec.md Tabs section mentions 'plain' for inactive; tabs.go line ~215 uses theme.Colors.TextMuted for inactive tabs

summary: PASS. The Tabs widget fully implements VAL-CMP-006: colored underline active indicator (not font-weight-only), keyboard navigation with forward/back/wrap/Shift-Tab/Home/End, focused vs unfocused visual distinction, and comprehensive test coverage (27 unit + 5 snapshot tests). Code follows established patterns (options pattern, theme tokens, no raw colors, no determinism violations). Two minor non-blocking issues: moveFirst/moveLast fire onChange unconditionally, and dead code in the single-tab Shift+Tab branch.
